observations: [2026-06-19] Shipyard (also referred to as 'C-yard' — C for context) is the umbrella context-engineering layer for the agent's interaction with the Resumsify codebase. Six-pillar vision from user's October 2026 sketch: Context Isolation (containerized + redundant-call-elimination + frequency-caching), Real-Time Codebase Syncing, Multi-Layer Validation, Observable Backend Metrics. Captured in ADR-0037 (Proposed, 2026-06-19).

[2026-06-19] Slice is the foundational primitive (Phase 1). Topic-keyed JSON manifests at docs/c-yard/<slice>.json unifying WHY (semantics/gotchas/designIntent) + HOW (traversalRecipes[] with intent + tool-chain + expectedSurface) + VALIDATION (fileFingerprints sha1 per file) + PROVENANCE (minedFromSessions + evidence). Replaces the split between memory MCP server (WHY only) and scattered traversal knowledge (HOW lives in chat transcripts + agent muscle memory + nowhere durable).

[2026-06-19] Memory MCP server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory@0.6.3 patched + NSSM-supervised at MCPMemorySupervisor on ports 3717/3718/3719) becomes legacy read-fallback during Phase 1 transition. Deprecated once every entity has a slice home. Operational tax (503 Single-client backing server, JSONL corruption recovery, NSSM patching ceremony) becomes bounded transition cost rather than permanent overhead.

[2026-06-19] Three open Slice schema decisions deferred to ADR-0038 sprint kickoff: (1) cross-slice relations storage shape (denormalized per-slice vs _index.json adjacency); (2) global / cross-cutting knowledge home (_global slice vs userMemory); (3) scope tiers (mirror MCP scopes resumsify/global/user-profile vs repo-only). Do NOT author any docs/c-yard/*.json file before ADR-0038 locks these.

[2026-06-19] Phase delivery is 6 phases (roadmap at docs/plans/shipyard-roadmap.md). Phase 0 shipped (codegraph + memory + analyzer + era cohorts via ADR-0011 + ADR-0036). Phase 1 = Slice unification (next, ADR-0038). Phase 2 = cached tool outputs in slices (ADR-0039). Phase 3 = frequency caching / preload telemetry (ADR-0040). Phase 4 = file-watcher push invalidation (first phase justifying a daemon — ADR-0041). Phase 5 = background diff worker on git HEAD (ADR-0042). Phase 6 = per-Slice observability dashboard (ADR-0043).

[2026-06-19] Chat-export analyzer (scripts/analyze-chat-exports.mjs from ADR-0036) is Shipyard's training pipeline. Phase 1 adds --mine-traversals <slice> flag: heuristic (toolName, normalizedArgs) tuples appearing in ≥2 reviewed sessions with no fallback grep_search within 3 turns → emits candidates to docs/c-yard/_candidates/<slice>.candidates.json. Human curates → promotes to canonical <slice>.json. Same human-in-the-loop discipline that keeps memory graph shallow.

[2026-06-19] Phase 0 read order at runtime (post-Phase-1): docs/c-yard/<slice>.json FIRST → mcp_memory open_nodes only as legacy fallback for un-migrated entities → codegraph_context for symbols not yet sliced → read_file targeted reads. Phase 0 instruction in compliance.instructions.md must be updated as part of Phase 1 commit 3 to add the slice-first lookup step.

[2026-06-19] First slice candidate is docs/c-yard/worklog-editor.json — densest existing memory entity (WorklogDomain + sub-entities in worklog.json shard), highest re-use signal in chat exports. Migration order by domain hotness: worklog-editor → worklog-draft-system → contacts/persona → asset-library → tiptap-yjs-integration. Migration script scripts/memory-to-slice.mjs (to be written in Phase 1 commit 4) reads docs/memory/<shard>.json shards and emits per-topic slice files.
